newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME live cattle end lower, feeders down.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME live cattle end lower, feeders down.

text.p: Nearby CME live cattle futures closed lower, with late selling motivated by doubts cash prices will move above $70 per cwt, traders said.

Futures traders have anticipated $70 cash cattle trades since last week and priced that into futures. By midday, USDA reported a few specialty cattle sold in Kansas at $70.50 per cwt, but otherwise trading was insufficient to establish prices.

Trading was light to moderate in live cattle, with gains impeded by underlying disappointment that October and December have been unable to hold near contract highs set Tuesday in October and Wednesday in December.
USDA reported beef cutout values were unchanged to up $0.26 per cwt in USDA's 1130 CDT report on sales of 187 loads.

Feeder cattle futures turned lower during the session in reaction to the upturn in CBOT corn futures. CBOT corn turned higher amid weather forecasts for below-normal temperatures in the Midwest next week. The late-planted crop needs warm weather to speed development.

Live cattle closed down 0.375 cent to up 0.125 cent with October off the most at 71.350 cents per lb. Feeder cattle were off 0.600 to up 0.150 with September off 0.325 at 63.300 and October off 0.600 at 63.450 cents.
